narrative.overview: GoodGround is a small team building real websites for real South African businesses, and the site is styled to look like exactly that: hands doing the work, not a stock-lifestyle mood board. The homepage hero is a photograph of the actual studio, not staged lifestyle photography, and every claim on the page is checkable (case studies link to live, testable URLs; unproven work says 'coming soon' rather than inventing a number). The palette is confident and unhedged rather than safe: a saturated signal orange against a warm paper cream, with a near-black purple for depth and gravity. There is no muted, corporate, 'trustworthy blue' register here, and no soft pastel wash either. Typography is Parkinsans for every heading paired with Instrument Sans for body copy, which stays plain and gets out of the way. Depth comes from one recurring device rather than shadows: a solid layer of orange sits offset behind a white or purple card, so the card appears to float slightly up and to the right of its own base.
keyCharacteristics: Photography is real, not stock: the studio, the actual product builds, the actual team.
One accent colour (orange) carries every primary action, at full saturation, with no muted variant.
Depth is an offset solid layer, not a blurred shadow.
Motion always eases out, never bounces, and every tap gets a visible press response.
Nothing is invented: no placeholder stats, no fabricated client logos, no 'trusted by' bar with no names in it.

rules.name: The Surface-Decides Rule
rules.body: Orange text passes contrast on Workshop Purple (4.50:1) and fails on Studio Paper or white (3.25:1). Crimson is the reverse. Never pick the accent colour by habit; pick it by what's underneath it.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: There is one primary accent, not a family of accent shades picked per section. If a component needs 'a slightly different orange,' the real answer is almost always Ember Crimson, not a new hex value.

rules.name: The Balance Rule
rules.body: Every h1-h4 gets text-wrap: balance globally, and paragraphs get text-wrap: pretty. Ragged headline line-lengths and single-word orphans are a defect, fixed at the base-layer level.

rules.name: The Tight-Tracking Rule
rules.body: Headings carry -0.02em letter-spacing as a base-layer default. Parkinsans at display sizes reads slightly loose without it.

rules.name: The Offset-Edge Rule
rules.body: A card's depth comes from a second, solid-colour layer positioned directly behind it and offset down-and-left by 6-7px, rather than from a blurred box-shadow.

dos: Do pick the accent colour (orange vs. crimson vs. purple) by what surface it sits on, per the Surface-Decides Rule, every time.
Do use the offset-edge treatment as the default depth answer for a new card before reaching for a shadow.
Do add active:scale-[0.97] (or equivalent press feedback) to every new interactive element.
Do gate every animation on prefers-reduced-motion, both globally and per-component.
Do keep claims checkable: link to something real, or say 'coming soon.' Never invent a stat, a client count, or a testimonial.
donts: Don't put white text on a Signal Orange background at normal text sizes; it fails WCAG AA.
Don't introduce a bounce or elastic easing curve anywhere.
Don't reach for a soft blurred shadow as a card's primary depth cue on the newer homepage sections.
Don't add a kicker/eyebrow label above a heading reflexively.
Don't ship a component that skips the prefers-reduced-motion gate, even for something that feels purely decorative.
